name: Corporate Investment Visa
description: The D-8 visa is for foreign entrepreneurs and investors establishing or investing in Korean businesses. It enables foreign nationals to start companies, invest in existing businesses, or manage Korean operations.
targetAudience: Foreign entrepreneurs starting businesses in Korea

workPermission.notes: Can hire employees and operate business freely

pathsTo.name: Residence Visa
pathsTo.requirements: Meet F-2-99 investment criteria or F-2-7 points system (80+). Business must be operational and demonstrate economic contribution.
pathsTo.notes: D-8 holders can qualify through the investment route (F-2-99) or the standard points system (F-2-7). F-2 provides more flexibility — you can work for any company or maintain your business.

pathsTo.name: Job Seeking Visa
pathsTo.requirements: Business closure or change in business status. Must have bachelor's degree. Apply before D-8 expires.
documents: Business closure documents or status change proof
pathsTo.notes: A fallback if your business venture ends and you want to seek employment instead. D-10 gives you up to 2 years to find a new path.

pathsFrom.name: Digital Nomad Visa (Workcation)
pathsFrom.requirements: Register a business in Korea with minimum investment. Must transition from remote work to Korean business operations.
pathsFrom.notes: For digital nomads who want to incorporate their business in Korea. Some nomads transition by establishing a Korean entity for their existing remote business.

pathsFrom.name: Job Seeking Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Must register a business in Korea with minimum investment. Transition from job seeking to entrepreneurship.
pathsFrom.notes: For D-10 holders who decide to start a business rather than seek employment. The investment threshold is significant (~₩100M).
